findings.title: Deauthentication burst from c0:ff:ee:00:00:01
findings.detail: 9 deauthenticate/disassociate frames in this capture, aimed at 2 address(es), including the broadcast address, which disconnects every client at once. This is how a client is forced off a network, either to deny it service or to make it reconnect so the handshake can be captured. A busy AP shedding idle clients can also produce these, so check whether one address is the source of all of them.

findings.title: 2 addresses appear to be one device
findings.detail: The addresses differ but the probe-request signature (and transmitter clock, where measured) match, which is what MAC randomisation on one handset looks like. Counting these as separate devices would overstate how many are present.
findings.evidence: identical probe-request element signature and transmitter clock offset within 2500 Hz and one sequence-number counter continuing across the address change -- one device rotating its MAC address
